skill.description: Explores Feishu and Lark OpenAPI documentation when existing Lark skills or lark-cli commands do not cover a request.

skill.author: larksuite

security_audit.summary: Most static backtick detections are Markdown formatting false positives, but several entries describe real lark-cli command workflows. The skill also relies on official Feishu and Lark documentation fetches and contains out-of-package sibling skill references. No prompt-injection attempt was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.suggestion: Inline the required shared safety rules or declare a packaged dependency instead of asking agents to read ../ sibling paths.
Require an explicit preview that restates target IDs, method, path, scopes, and expected impact before any mutating request.
Constrain WebFetch use to official Feishu and Lark domains and avoid following user-supplied documentation URLs.
Label examples as templates and require users to approve concrete values before execution with lark-cli.

content.value_statement: Teams often need Lark API actions that are not wrapped by existing skills. This skill finds official endpoint details and helps call them through lark-cli.
actual_capabilities: Checks whether an existing Lark skill or lark-cli command already covers the request.
Fetches Feishu or Lark OpenAPI index pages from official documentation URLs.
Locates module documents and endpoint documents for a requested Lark task.
Extracts methods, paths, parameters, scopes, responses, and error notes from API documentation.
Shows how to call GET, POST, PUT, and DELETE endpoints with lark-cli api.
Translates Chinese documentation details when the user is working in English.
limitations: Requires lark-cli to be installed and authenticated before API calls can work.
Depends on current Feishu or Lark documentation being reachable and accurate.
Does not guess undocumented paths, parameters, or permissions.
Write and delete operations require explicit user confirmation before execution.

use_cases.title: Find an Unwrapped Chat API
use_cases.description: Locate the official endpoint for a chat action that lark-cli does not expose directly.

use_cases.title: Prepare an API Call Plan
use_cases.description: Collect required parameters, scopes, and request constraints before running a sensitive Lark operation.

use_cases.title: Translate API Documentation
use_cases.description: Turn Chinese Feishu OpenAPI documentation into concise English implementation notes.

prompt_templates.title: Find a Lark Endpoint
prompt_templates.prompt: Find the official Lark OpenAPI endpoint for this task: [describe task]. Check existing lark-cli coverage first.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize Required Inputs
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the official Feishu documentation to list the method, path, required parameters, permissions, and key errors for [task].

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Safe Call
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare the lark-cli api call for [task]. Ask for confirmation before any write, update, or delete operation.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Candidate APIs
prompt_templates.prompt: Search the Lark OpenAPI docs for APIs related to [workflow]. Compare candidates and recommend the safest endpoint.

output_examples.input: Find how to add users to a Lark chat when no wrapped command exists.
output_examples.output: The skill identifies the chat member endpoint, lists required identifiers and permissions, and asks for confirmation before adding members.

output_examples.input: Explain the API for updating a chat announcement in English.
output_examples.output: The skill summarizes the endpoint purpose, required revision value, announcement content format, permissions, and expected response behavior.

output_examples.input: Check whether an existing command can handle a messaging task.
output_examples.output: The skill first reviews available lark-cli messaging commands, then uses OpenAPI documentation only if no direct command exists.

best_practices: Start with existing lark-cli help before exploring raw OpenAPI endpoints.
Use official Feishu or Lark documentation as the source of truth for every parameter.
Confirm target resources, scopes, and expected impact before running mutating calls.
anti_patterns: Do not guess API paths or request bodies from memory.
Do not run POST, PUT, PATCH, or DELETE operations without explicit confirmation.
Do not follow non-official API documentation links for endpoint discovery.

faq.question: What problem does this skill solve?
faq.answer: It helps find native Lark OpenAPI endpoints when existing skills or lark-cli commands do not cover a task.

faq.question: Does it require lark-cli?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is designed to call endpoints through lark-cli api after discovery.

faq.question: Can it make changes in a Lark workspace?
faq.answer: Yes, if the user confirms a write operation and the authenticated account has the required permissions.

faq.question: Which documentation sources does it use?
faq.answer: It uses official Feishu and Lark OpenAPI documentation indexes and endpoint pages.

faq.question: Can English users use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill instructs the assistant to translate Chinese documentation details into English when needed.

faq.question: Does it replace official API review?
faq.answer: No. Users should still verify permissions, target identifiers, and operation impact before execution.
